chunks: The gazing of people’s eyes is not hidden from Him, nor the repetition of words, nor the glimpse of hillocks, nor the tread of a footstep in the dark night or in the deep gloom, where the shining moon casts its light and the effulgent sun comes in its wake, through its setting and appearing again and again with the rotation of time and periods, by the approach of the advancing night or the passing away of the running day. He precedes every extremity and limit, and every counting and numbering.

key_terms.ازْدِلَافُ رَبْوَةٍ: The glimpse or view of a hillock
key_terms.انْبِسَاطُ خُطْوَةٍ: The tread or step of a foot
key_terms.ذَاتُ النُّورِ: The possessor of light (referring to the sun)
key_terms.شُخُوصُ لَحْظَةٍ: The gazing or glancing of the eye
key_terms.كُرُورُ لَفْظَةٍ: The repetition or recurrence of a word

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about God's knowledge of time and subtle movements?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia theological discourse, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha underscores the concept of 'Ilm al-Ilahi' (Divine Knowledge) as an eternal, non-temporal attribute of God, distinct from human cognitive processes. It highlights the Imam's rhetorical mastery in using cosmic imagery—such as the moon and sun—to illustrate that God's awareness transcends the physical mechanisms of time and space, a key tenet in distinguishing His essence from creation.
